fixes.explanation: No riverside in this passage, friend. The text says Paul reasoned in the synagogue, and in the marketplace with those he met each day. Every day! I couldn't talk to people daily by a river, because the first time somebody asked me a hard question I'd be standing there with nowhere to go. The marketplace is the answer, because that's where the people were.

Wars don't come up in this speech, friend. Paul says God has set a day when He “…will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed.” So the day is about justice, and the Man He appointed is the one doing the judging. Then Paul backs it up: God “…has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.” That's why he tells them to repent in verse 30.

Yes, Damaris. The text says some joined Paul and believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite, “…a woman named Damaris, and others who were with them.” Think about that room, friend. Some of the crowd had just mocked Paul, and she heard the very same sermon and believed. Her name made it into the Bible, and I'd say that's a pretty good place to end up.
